editorial:
Imagine your favorite powerhouse hero getting an even bigger upgrade. That is exactly what happens here as you follow Ultraman Zero in a race against time to save the galaxy. The vibe is high-energy from the very first scene, mixing classic giant monster fights with a fresh story about pushing past your own limits. You get to see Zero struggle with his powers before he unlocks the Ultra Cosmo Records, and the excitement builds perfectly as he discovers how to use the new UltRise Eye to channel the strength of past legends. It feels like a big celebration of everything that makes the Ultra series great.

What really hits home is the action choreography by Koichi Sakamoto, which keeps the pacing fast and the fights feeling huge. While some of the plot points are a bit predictable, the flashy visuals and emotional moments make up for it. If you are a fan of big battles and flashy transformations, you need to see this. To get the best experience, you should definitely stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video to see all the light effects, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for your physical collection if you love owning your movies.
endingExplained: In the final battle, Zero realizes that the UltRise Eye is not just a tool, but a bridge to all the Ultra Heroes. He combines their spirits to reach a new level of power, completely wiping out the main villain with a massive cosmic beam. After the fight, he returns the borrowed strength to the stars, proving he has grown as a leader. The movie wraps up with Zero looking toward the horizon, ready for his next adventure.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves giant monster battles and epic hero transformations.
